pivot: Whether the settled root-cause finding lands at the model layer (fault reproducible across system prompts / independent of operator configuration) or the deployment layer (operator-specific misuse or misconfiguration)
pivot_observable: The published root-cause/attribution finding's own characterization of where the fault sits — whether it states the failure mode is reproducible on the base model regardless of operator wrapping, or specific to the named operator's deployment
pivot_because: pressure-model argues the developer is the target 'because the developer holds the only lever whose next-choice derivative actually changes future harm' — that only holds if the fault traces to something the developer controls. ai-incident-severity argues remediation ships 'regardless of where the settled root-cause finding lands' — which is itself an argument about this exact variable, asserting it doesn't matter, rather than evidence it doesn't. Neither minute names the observable directly, but both are visibly arguing opposite faces of it. If root cause lands at the deployment layer, the developer has no lever to pull and no exposure to price in — lab-moves, ai-incident-severity, ai-pressure, and pressure-model all lose their actor and their claims dissolve or transfer to the operator. If it lands at the model layer, all four claims are live simultaneously. That is a reordering of the outcome set, not a shift in confidence within one.
rival_pivots_rejected: Product move vs. political move (ai-pressure vs. lab-moves/ai-incident-severity): ai-pressure's own round-2 DEFEND concedes a lab can do both simultaneously — a capability restriction and a political endorsement are not exclusive branches, so resolving this shifts which move gets more emphasis, not which outcomes are reachable. Developer-alone vs. developer+operator pair (pressure-model vs. ai-public-backlash): this is real disagreement but it is downstream of the root-cause pivot — it only becomes decidable once you know whether the operator has any independent exposure, which is exactly what root-cause layer settles. Enforcer-with-standing vs. no enforcer (ai-regulation-teeth): orthogonal axis — it is about which *institution* imposes cost, not about who the target is, and its six-month window runs regardless of which layer the fault sits in.
ruling: The developer becomes the concentrated target of both product remediation and pressure-model dynamics only if the root-cause finding places fault at the model layer; if it places fault at the deployment layer, the operator inherits the exposure and the developer's obligation narrows to cooperation, not remediation.
because: pressure-model's lever argument and ai-incident-severity's 'regardless of layer' claim are the two strongest, most specific minutes, and they are arguing directly opposite sides of the same unstated variable — one says it matters, one says it doesn't. ai-public-backlash's revised claim (naming the developer/operator pair) is the minute that best captures what happens if the deployment layer is where fault lands: the operator stays a named target instead of dropping out. lab-moves and ai-incident-severity both presuppose the developer is the exposed party without arguing for it, which is why the root-cause layer, not '30 days vs quantified-loss' timing, is what actually decides whether their claims fire.
threat_live: What becomes newly dangerous on this branch is a fault that survives arbitrary system prompts (model-layer, per ai-incident-severity) going unremediated because the 'isolated to the operator' defense is asserted and, this time, actually holds — displacing consequence onto the operator while capability elsewhere in the model line stays unchanged (lab-moves' own carve-out). What becomes newly safe is the developer's own exposure, if root cause truly is deployment-specific: no product concession, no political concession, just cooperation with an operator-directed enforcement action.
strongest_minute: ai-regulation-teeth — it offers one clean, checkable discriminator (does an entity with pre-existing standing file by 2027-03-31) that is true regardless of which side of the root-cause pivot the case falls on, and it explicitly distinguishes rule-that-bites from theater rather than conflating the two.
weakest_minute: ai-pressure — its claim is nested inside an unproven premise ('if the incident's operator/developer sits inside the named frontier set already carrying saturated pressure') and further assumes a specific named bill (Thune/Cruz/Klobuchar) is live and endorsable, neither of which the brief granted; it also concedes in round 2 that its own 'cheapest exit' framing may not be singular.
shared_assumption: ai-pressure, pressure-model, and ai-incident-severity all import the same internal pressure-framework vocabulary (P6, 'saturated' pressure, '10.5 installed pressure', 'tension 0.66', Σ p(b)·|∂L/∂choice|) without arguing for the framework itself — this is one shared model of how pressure converts to action wearing three slugs, not three independent confirmations.
smuggled_assumption: ai-pressure assumes a specific federal bill (Thune/Cruz/Klobuchar) is live, credible, and endorsable by 2026-12-17 — the brief granted an incident and an ordering, not the existence of a particular pending bill.
unresolved: The minutes never state whether the root-cause finding will characterize fault by layer (model vs. deployment) at all, or whether attribution processes typically produce a finding granular enough to settle this — lab-moves in particular presupposes developer exposure without ever arguing why the fault should trace to the model rather than the operator's use of it.
